name: Build Your Own Regex
description: Implement a regular expression engine from scratch, supporting literal matching, character classes, quantifiers, and backtracking.
readme:
# Build Your Own Regex

Implement a regular expression engine in Rust, inspired by regular-expressions.info.

## Stages

1. Literal Matching: Match exact strings character by character
2. Character Classes: Support \d, \w, \s, ., and [abc] / [a-z] ranges
3. Quantifiers: Support *, +, ?, and {n,m} greedy and lazy matching
4. Backtracking: Implement a backtracking NFA engine for full regex support

## Getting Started

Each stage builds on the previous one. Start with stage 1.

Run `cargo test` after implementing each stage.

stages.description: Match exact strings character by character. Support anchoring with ^ and $.

stages.name: Stage 2: Character Classes
stages.description: Support \d, \w, \s, dot, and character class syntax [abc], [a-z].

stages.name: Stage 4: Backtracking
stages.description: Implement a full backtracking NFA engine supporting all regex constructs including groups and captures.
